To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maturity stages of IT in South Korea are defined by using the L&K model and that the benchmarks of each stage have been validated.
IT maturity stages are empirically defined and validated, and significant benchmarking data are presented to support the defined maturity stages.

(1) the IT maturity stages of Korean enterprises have been validated through a statistical test; (2) the benchmarks for each stage are defined and confirmed; (3) the benchmarks of the IT maturity stage can be used for enterprise benchmarking; and (4) IT maturity stages and enterprise benchmarks can be used for managerial implications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework for the evaluation of the maturity of the information technology (IT) in an organization.
the development of a framework for the assessment of information technology (I.T.) maturity in the context of the public sector.
the development of a model of the relationship between information technology (IT) and the firm's business performance.

there is a significant difference between the two groups of enterprises in terms of their IT maturity levels.

IT maturity stage 1 is characterized by a lack of IT planning, IT infrastructure, and IT personnel; stage 2 by a lack of strategic alignment of IT; stage 3 by a lack of integration of IT and business processes; and stage 4 by a lack of a comprehensive approach to IT governance.

the L&K model is a valid model of IT maturity stages, and that the benchmarks for each stage are significant.Originality/value – The L&K model has been widely applied in IT evaluation studies, but the model has not been confirmed by statistical testing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IT evaluation model based on IT maturity stage is valid and that IT benchmarking can be conducted through the stages model.
we have developed a new model that is based on the L&K model, but that has the advantage of being more comprehensive and that has been validated through a large scale survey.

the results show that the maturity stage of the organization is a significant factor in the use of information technology and the level of information technology maturity in an organization has a significant influence on the use of information technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the maturity stages theory is a valid and reliable method to evaluate IT maturity in enterprises.
the maturity of IT is not only a function of the level of IT adoption, but also a function of the way the organization uses the IT to support its business.
, in general, the more mature the company, the more likely it is to be using the latest IT.
